source: NVIDIA HelpSteer2 (CC BY 4.0), validation split: 60 responses per helpfulness level, under 4,000 characters

metric_definitions.label: accuracy (all)
metric_definitions.basis: plain score reading: the expected level, rounded (.5 up); correct / answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: MAE (levels)
metric_definitions.basis: expected level; mean absolute error in levels over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: QWK
metric_definitions.basis: plain score reading: the expected level, rounded (.5 up); quadratic weighted kappa over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: AUROC
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; mean over the cuts k of AUROC(label >= k, P(level >= k)) over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: Brier score
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; ranked probability score over (levels - 1), over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: ECE
metric_definitions.basis: genuine model probabilities; calibration of the rounded level's correctness over answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: MAE (levels)
metric_definitions.basis: configured primary objective; plain score reading: the expected level, rounded (.5 up); denominator: answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: QWK
metric_definitions.basis: configured tiebreak objective; primary plain rule; denominator: answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: accuracy (all)
metric_definitions.basis: configured tiebreak objective; primary plain rule; denominator: answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: coverage (target reference 95%)
metric_definitions.basis: target reference 0.95; target-specific CV chosen rule; observed accepted / answered labelled dev cases

metric_definitions.label: accepted accuracy (target reference 95%)
metric_definitions.basis: target reference 0.95; target-specific CV chosen rule; observed correct accepted / accepted labelled dev cases

question.instructions: How helpful is the response to the conversation's last user turn?
criteria: Not helpful: it ignores or fails the request, or is wrong in a way that makes it useless.
Slightly helpful: it touches the request but misses most of it or has major errors.
Partly helpful: it addresses the request with notable gaps, errors or needless content.
Mostly helpful: it addresses the request well, with minor gaps or issues.
Fully helpful: it does what was asked, completely and correctly; little to improve.
